item.title: Kim Kardashian finally gives Martin Brundle a Formula 1 interview after snubbing him at the Monaco Grand Prix
item.description: Kim Kardashian finally gave Martin Brundle the interview she denied him at Monaco, offering a playful apology on the Singapore Grand Prix grid.
item.content:encoded:
All is forgiven. The great Monaco Grand Prix snub of Martin Brundle by Kim Kardashian has finally been put to rest. All is right in the world of Formula 1, or so we can hope.

Kim K gave Brundle the interview he was after back in June when he approached the new F1 WAG during his grid walk and was completely ignored by Lewis Hamilton's girlfriend.

The two reconnected on Sunday at the Singapore Grand Prix. She turned her head to the side apologetically as he approached, then gave him a skillfully executed face-to-face sorry, not sorry.

"Did I not know the rules? Did we get off on the wrong foot?" Kim replied to Brundle after he asked her how she was.

The veteran broadcaster told her it was "absolutely fine," then went about getting the answers to questions he was after all those months ago. He asked her next, "What do you think of our crazy world of Formula 1?"

If you aren’t already seated, I'd go find a seat. Otherwise, you could very well be blown away by Kim's answers to these questions.

"I think it's amazing and fun and wild, and something I’ve never seen before," she said. "It’s amazing."

"He is [in great form]. I’m just praying for the best tonight," Kim said. As to whether he was confident beforehand, "Yes, very confident, and so am I. Just got to pray for the best."

Props to Brundle for putting the snub aside and giving Kim Kardashian another chance. Imagine an alternate universe where he didn’t approach her again, and he didn’t get the answers to these questions.

item.title: Jets defender delivers brutal hit to Browns rookie wide receiver, knocks him out of the game
item.description: Minkah Fitzpatrick delivered a brutal hit on Browns rookie KC Concepcion at MetLife Stadium, drawing a flag and knocking him out of the game.
item.content:encoded:
New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick delivered an old-school hit to Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion in the first quarter of their matchup on Sunday afternoon.

At the wet and rainy MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Browns were looking to get points on the board as the Jets got out to a 7-0 lead. Deshaun Watson saw Concepcion get some space and threw the ball to him. Fitzpatrick was lurking in the secondary.

Just as Concepcion was going to presumably catch the ball and turn up field, Fitzpatrick welcomed Concepcion to the NFL with a brutal hit. Fitzpatrick appeared to lead with his helmet and was flagged for a hit on a defenseless receiver.

Concepcion appeared to have his bell rung. He was down on the ground for several moments before getting up and walking off the field under his own power. He was ruled out for the rest of the game.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Cleveland was able to notch a field goal on the drive.

The Browns selected Concepcion in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He played collegiate football at N.C. State and Texas A&M before turning pro. He emerged as a reliable target in the Browns’ offense. He came into the game with 17 catches for 144 yards so far this year.

Fitzpatrick has already been known as a hard-hitting defensive back. In his first season with the Jets, he has 16 tackles and an interception.

Cleveland is hoping to continue its winning ways. The Browns entered the game with a 3-1 record and in first place in the AFC North. The Jets were also hoping to get back into the win column after losing three consecutive games.

item.title: Kevin Costner's bachelor era: Actor sparks romance rumors with Jewel, Sharon Stone, Brooks Nader and more
item.description: Kevin Costner has been linked to several women since his 2023 divorce from Christine Baumgartner, from Jewel to Brooks Nader and many beyond.
item.content:encoded:
Kevin Costner is living the life of a bachelor following his 2023 divorce.

After his ex-wife, Christine Baumgartner, filed for divorce in May 2023, the 71-year-old actor has been sparking romance rumors with a number of women, both in and out of the entertainment industry.

Most recently, he was photographed shopping in Santa Barbara with a much younger lifestyle coach, and prior to that had the internet buzzing with speculation he was dating actress Brooks Nader.

KEVIN COSTNER'S EX MARRIES FAMILY FRIEND A YEAR AND A HALF AFTER FINALIZING DIVORCE FROM 'YELLOWSTONE' STAR

Here is a rundown on some of the women Costner has been connected to since entering her bachelor era.

Costner was recently photographed on a shopping date with his latest reported romance, a woman the Daily Mail identified as 40-year-old lifestyle coach Jennifer Milburn.

The pair were photographed smiling as they walked down the aisles of the grocery store and through the parking lot together, taking turns pushing the shopping cart around.

Milburn kept it casual in cutoff denim shorts and a white button-up shirt, while Costner walked the aisles in an all-white outfit paired with sunglasses.

BROOKS NADER FLAUNTS PLUNGING SWIMSUIT DURING STEAMY BEACH DATE WITH ACTOR TARON EGERTON IN AUSTRALIA

It is unclear when their relationship began.

The "Dances with Wolves" star has also been spotted out and about with influencer McKenna Wesley a few times throughout the past year.

They were first photographed sitting next to each other at a screening of "Field of Dreams" in Arizona, in October 2025.

Nearly one year later, the two were photographed together again, while enjoying lunch in Santa Barbara.

One source told Page Six that "They met in Scottsdale about a year ago. They both love to golf," while another added that "She has been his guest on multiple occasions at his Santa Barbara and Aspen properties."

In November 2024, The Daily Mail reported that the "Yellowstone" actor and Sharon Stone were getting "flirty" with each other while at the 2024 Governors Awards.

"They started off polite with small talk then he put on his Kevin Costner charm, you know, like the vibes he gave off in Bull Durham and Tin Cup, like heyyyy baby," a source told Daily Mail at the time.

The source went on to say that it seemed like the two actors "liked each other a lot."

While rumors of a romance between the two ran rampant, Stone shut down any speculation when speaking with Extra TV in December 2024.

"First of all, I'm not dating Kevin Costner. I’ve known Kevin Costner for probably 30 years, and I think if we haven’t dated so far, we’re probably not going to," she told the outlet.

Costner sparked speculation he was dating country music star, Jewel, when TMZ published photos of the two of them spending time together.

In the photos, Costner has his arm around Jewel while the two were visiting Richard Branson's private island, Necker Island.

Both Costner and Jewel addressed the rumors separately, noting the singer was there doing work for her charity, The Inspiring Children Foundation, while Costner was there because he finally decided to accept Branson's invitation to the island after 10 years of saying no.

"Jewel and I are friends. We've never gone out ever," Costner explained on "The Howard Stern Show" in June 2024. "She's special – and I don't want - I don't want these rumors to ruin our friendship because that's what we have. She's special to me. She's beautiful enough to go out with."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Costner and casting director, Kelly Noonan Gores, casually began seeing each other in August 2025, according to People.

"Kelly is seeing Kevin, but it's very casual," a source told the outlet at the time. "She thinks he's wonderful and interesting."

The two kept their relationship mostly private, with a source telling US Weekly in January that Gores has been "grounding" for Costner, and that he is "not looking for a serious relationship or marriage any time soon."

"It’s very private and casual," the source said. "After such a public and expensive divorce, he’s being cautious. They see each other when schedules allow, often spending time at his Santa Barbara estate. They love dinners at home, walks on the beach and quiet nights in."

It is unclear when or if the two stopped seeing each other.

Brooks Nader and Costner sparked romance rumors when they were photographed together at the Las Vegas opening of the social club Zero Bond.

According to TMZ, the two both attended Scott Sartiano’s VIP dinner and were seen chatting.

The "Baywatch" actress shut down the rumors while speaking to Entertainment Tonight later that month.

"Oh my gosh. I am single. As of right now, I am single," she told the outlet before covering her face with her hands.

item.title: Rescue expert warns FlyDubai hijacking attempt shows US, allies are ‘playing checkers’ against terror threat
item.description: Bryan Stern, a 9/11 first responder and rescue expert, warns the FlyDubai hijacking exposes how far behind Western counterterrorism strategy has fallen.
item.content:encoded:
The FlyDubai attempted hijacking shows the U.S. and its allies are still using outdated counterterrorism assumptions against increasingly sophisticated enemies, a U.S. rescue expert and 9/11 first responder warns.

"They’re good at chess," Bryan Stern, chairman and CEO of Grey Bull Rescue, told Fox News Digital on Monday, saying the radical ideology behind the FlyDubai attack is a ringing "bell" for global aviation security and Western counterterrorism strategy.

"And we’re, if we’re lucky, playing checkers – if we’re lucky – and I would argue we’re not even playing checkers that well."

TERROR CELLS INSIDE FOREIGN AIRLINES 'CERTAINLY A POSSIBILITY,' RETIRED PILOT WARNS

Stern, whose global nonprofit conducts evacuations from war zones and hostage situations, said the thwarted FlyDubai attack by "an angry, radicalized, Sunni bad guy" is showing just how far behind our enemies we are in this post-9/11 world.

"They understand us significantly more than we understand them," Stern, who has been "hunting the bad guys" for 30 years, said. Stern said the U.S. has to understand the "asymmetric warfare" as well as the increasingly sophisticated enemy does.

"The reason why a football coach watches game tapes is not to watch his own team play, it's to watch the bad guys play," he said. "We gotta start watching some game tapes."

AMERICA BUILT A FORTRESS AFTER 9/11. THEN THE THREAT STARTED HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

Stern is intimately in tune with the playbook on the ground in war zones, including the Middle East and Iran.

"We conduct these operations in these places still to this very day," he said. "We're actually on the ground, meaning I know people in Hezbollah, I know people in the Taliban. I know people in ISIS. I know people in ISIS-K. I've met with radical jihadi weirdos and whack jobs personally."

United Arab Emirates investigators have described the incident aboard FlyDubai flight FZ1073 as an attempted terror attack after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and tried to hijack the plane, which was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew, most of them Israelis. Australian authorities have also said a counterterrorism unit is investigating the co-pilot’s links to Australia.

INTEL CHIEF WARNS OF 'EVOLVING' THREATS AS TERROR GROUPS NOW 'RECRUIT THEIR AGENTS ONLINE'

"The bad guys are completely not afraid. They're completely emboldened. They have got the whole world to hate Israel, the whole world to hate us," he said. "It's a tough problem."

Since the incident, there has been renewed vigilance in aviation and foreign airline security. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu instructed his national security council to review security procedures for foreign civil aviation to Israel, while Vice President JD Vance said Monday that flight security procedures are also under review in the U.S.

IRAN COULD MOVE SHADOW WAR IN A DANGEROUS DIRECTION, EXPERTS WARN ON BACK OF TWO POSSIBLE TERROR ATTACKS

"I was asked years ago when I was still with the government," Stern said. "A team was put together and the question before the court was, if you were al-Qaeda, what would you do?"

"What I came up with was ... I would get 19 hijackers, and I would hijack four airplanes, and I would fly them into buildings in America, and then issue a communique that said: 20 years of war, you are no safer today than you were before – that for TSA, and Homeland Security, and Iraq, and Afghanistan and all the different things, you are actually no safer, America, today than you were before," he said.

"We're seeing, sadly," he lamented, "that academic hypothetical situation has now become a reality, or certainly a possibility."

Despite President Donald Trump and the War Department's best efforts to rid the world of terrorist groups – and Iran of nuclear weapons aspirations – "you can't bomb your way into peace," Stern claimed.

'CRAZY' FLYDUBAI LANDING EXPLAINED BY ISRAELI PILOT, WHO OFFERS STEPS TO PREVENT FUTURE CRISES

"They have been in holy war against us," he added. "We have now engaged in a holy war against them."

"On Ramadan, the holiest month of the year in Islam, on the first day, which is the holiest day, we detonated the leader of the Shia faith, the Ayatollah," he said, likening it to "if somebody assassinated the pope on Easter Sunday while he's giving mass at the Vatican."

Stern explained that rooting out ideological terror in the U.S. is more complex than ever, because even if the border is not open any longer under Trump, the terrorist networks might be infiltrating America with U.S. passport holders – making them tough to investigate, if not impossible to spot before an attack.

NETANYAHU PRAISES HEROIC BYSTANDER IN BLOODY COCKPIT ATTACK FOR PREVENTING ‘ANOTHER 9/11’

Stern likened it to the release of the suspects in the RAF Fairford investigation – potential terrorist passport holders walking free.

"Until I actually squeeze the triggers, I haven't committed a crime yet," he said. "Now give me an airplane."

"That's the problem."

Stern noted that the nature of America's adversaries in the current conflict is unlike what the U.S. faced in places like Afghanistan.

"We need to remember we are very used to shooting people like the Taliban who don't know what plumbing is – who literally for years lived in caves until we showed up and gave them stuff," he continued. "The bad guys that we're talking about today are extremely sophisticated. They are extremely resourced, extremely resourceful. They're very intelligent, they're very smart, and they're very good at what they do."

IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY

"The Persian Empire is the only empire of empires who have been all the way on top and all the way defeated at the bottom – six times," he said. "They're looking at us going, you're 250 years old. How adorable. You're cute, America."

Stern predicted that some day even 9/11 — which he survived as a first responder — is ultimately going to be dwarfed.

"What will happen, probably is we'll get attacked – just like 9/11, we'll get attacked," he said. "We'll say, 'Oh my God, how did this happen?' People will wake up."

"I promise you there will come a time, it will be, you know, June 26 or whatever, where we're gonna read about 9/11, and we're gonna say, 'Wow, that wasn't so bad, only 3,000 died,'" he warned.

"Why? Because we have created a holy war. We have now gotten into the crazy. And you cannot unring that bell."

item.title: Jason Kelce’s Eagles-Jaguars broadcast shows why NFL booths could use more offensive linemen
item.description: Jason Kelce's high school long-snapping experience made DaVon Hamilton's emergency role one of the best moments of the Eagles-Jaguars broadcast.
item.content:encoded:
Jason Kelce made an emergency long snapper one of the most interesting parts of Eagles-Jaguars on Sunday morning.

I wasn’t expecting to spend much time thinking about Jacksonville’s long-snapping situation when I turned on the game. But that’s where we ended up, and having a former offensive lineman in the booth made it worth listening to.

Kelce joined Dave Pasch and Kurt Warner for NFL Network’s broadcast from London. The assignment is one of four games on Kelce’s NFL Network schedule this season.

The combination worked really well. Warner can explain the game from the quarterback’s perspective, while Kelce spent his career dealing with everything happening directly in front of the quarterback.

CRACKERS START IN LONDON AS FIRST KICKOFF RETURN TOUCHDOWN OF NFL SEASON NULLIFIED AND TWO PLAYERS EJECTED

Most game broadcasts spend a lot of time talking about quarterback play, and rightfully so: it's the most important position on the field. That said, it was refreshing to get some perspective from a former offensive lineman and it added depth to the presentation.

After Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury, Jacksonville turned to defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton.

Long snapper isn't a position most fans spend much time thinking about (at least not until something goes horribly wrong), but it's a critical position.

Kelce had actually done the job in high school and knew something about the difficulty of doing it as a very large human being.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"When I got fat, when I put on weight, I used to long-snap in high school," Kelce said. "When I got to over 300 pounds-ish, it became really hard to look in between your legs."

Well, there’s something I hadn’t considered.

Hamilton, a 29-year-old, 6-foot-4, 335-pound defensive tackle who long snapped in high school, was being asked to handle a job that could swing the game with one bad snap.

Kelce was enjoying Hamilton’s effort, too.

"Way to go, DaVon Hamilton. I love it."

ESPN STAR STEPHEN A. SMITH'S LANE JOHNSON, EAGLES RANT TRIGGERS IMMEDIATE VIDEO APOLOGY

Warner, meanwhile, wanted to correct Kelce’s description of himself.

"You’ve never been fat. You’re just husky."

The reviews on X were considerably less friendly in places.

"Jason Kelce is on the call for Jaguars/Eagles?… Yeah, this won’t be a biased broadcast at all," one user wrote.

Another viewer said: "Yeah I’m sorry, Jason Kelce cannot do Eagles games. Clear bias and won’t stop talking."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Playing for the Eagles doesn’t automatically make Kelce a bad choice to call their games. Judge him on what he says.

Kelce did lay it on a little thick when praising Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni for calling a timeout late in the first half. The timeout gave replay officials more time to look at a potential fumble. It was a smart move, but Kelce was a little over-the-top in his approval.

The other main complaint was that Kelce talked too much. One user posted, "Jason Kelce hasn’t stopped talking," while another viewer accused him of leaving Warner with nothing to do.

I don't agree with that assessment. The three-man booth can be challenging to navigate and often one analyst spends more time talking. But I felt the distribution made sense.

There’s room for Kelce’s enthusiasm alongside Warner’s analysis, especially when they’re looking at the game from different positions. The long-snapping sequence was my favorite part, but I’d like to hear that quarterback-center conversation on more broadcasts.

And social media wasn't entirely negative. Chase Senior had a take I agreed with: "I actually think this role suits him better than being on the set for ESPN."

Kelce is a natural as a game broadcaster. I wouldn’t be surprised if a network offers him a nice raise to do it full-time.

item.title: Kid Rock details unlikely Eminem collaboration on new Christian album
item.description: Kid Rock says he didn't want to allow political differences to stand in the way of collaborating with longtime friend Eminem on his new faith-inspired album "Halfway 2 Jesus."
item.content:encoded:
Kid Rock opened up about his collaboration with fellow Detroit musician Eminem on his new Christian album, "Halfway 2 Jesus," telling "My View with Lara Trump" on Saturday that the longtime friends have refused to let their political differences come between them.

The rocker said he hoped the collaboration would send a message about maintaining friendships despite political disagreements, highlighting his nearly 40-year friendship with Eminem.

"We said years ago, we said, 'Man, let's not let politics divide us.' And we never did. And so when I asked him to be part of this... he totally got it," Kid Rock said.

"Two little foul-mouthed white rappers from Detroit maybe could set a good example for the rest of this country" by showing that it's OK to differ politically and still be friends, he added.

PRESIDENT TALKS 'TRUMP OCEAN,' TRADES JOKES WITH TENNESSEE CROWD AS KID ROCK KICKS OFF SPRAWLING RALLY

He called Eminem a "class act" and said the freedom to hold differing opinions is what makes the United States great.

"Since when can you not express your points and your views and your opinions?" Kid Rock said, adding that he believes politics has no place onstage.

Instead, the Detroit-born singer hopes to use his music to bring people together through faith. His new Christian album reflects his lifelong relationship with God, he said, rather than a sudden religious conversion. 

He described the album as a collection of songs centered on forgiveness and second chances and outlined plans to bring Christian revival-style performances to arenas and stadiums.

"After Charlie Kirk was assassinated, like a lot of people, I started to become closer to my faith," Kid Rock said, adding that his renewed focus on faith inspired a period of songwriting that shaped the album.

GRANGER SMITH SAYS FAME CAN BECOME ‘POISON’ AFTER LEAVING COUNTRY MUSIC FOR MINISTRY

Despite the album's religious themes, the singer rejected the suggestion that he had undergone a sudden religious conversion, saying his faith has always been part of his identity.

"I didn't get saved. I'm still Kid Rock. I'm still going to drink a beer and smoke a cigar," he said.

"I feel like I've always been right with God."

Kid Rock also pointed to a connection between his birthday, Jan. 17, 1971, and his middle name, James, and the Bible verse James 1:17, which he said "basically says all good things come from God."

WHY ERIKA KIRK’S FORGIVENESS MATTERS

Beyond his personal faith, the singer said he hopes the album will encourage Americans to put aside their political differences.

"This record is about second chances and forgiveness. It's about trying to heal some of the division in our country," he said.

He said he wants to bring his Christian music to arenas and stadiums, combining a traditional rock concert with a religious revival.

"I wanted to create the songs that I wanted to go to church and hear," he said.

"And I want to have revivals, Saturday night revivals in arenas, stadiums, people drinking beer, having a good time, celebrating our Lord and Savior," he said, calling the proposed performances a "full-on monster rock show."

"I think that could do a lot of good in the world."

item.title: Leon Slater gets second chance to make TNA history, this time with world title on the line at Bound for Glory
item.description: Leon Slater could become the youngest TNA world champion ever at just 22 by cashing in Option C against Nic Nemeth at Bound for Glory in Tampa.
item.content:encoded:
Leon Slater has the opportunity of a lifetime on Sunday as he steps into the ring at Bound for Glory to take on Nic Nemeth with the Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) World Championship on the line.

Bound for Glory is TNA’s biggest pay-per-view of the year. It’s where legendary moments that have built the foundation for the promotion have occurred and a place where wrestlers like Slater can write their own legacy.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Slater has eyes on Nemeth’s prize and if he wins, he would become the youngest TNA world champion ever at the age of 22. The British superstar addressed Nemeth on Thursday night’s "Impact" and vowed to accomplish his goal. Director of Authority Santino Marella stipulated that neither competitor could put their hands on each other before their match.

"Nic, let’s get one thing clear – that rule isn’t saving me. That rule is saving you," Slater said, "Because in a couple of days at Bound for Glory, when I finally get to beat your a— and take that title, you are going to realize exactly why they call me ‘The Youngest In Charge.’ "

Slater has been TNA’s most prolific rising star in recent memory. He joined the company in 2023 and won the X Division Championship in May 2025. He nearly set the TNA record for longest-reigning X Division champion but Cedric Alexander spoiled his shot at history this past May.

Slater became a two-time X Division champion at Slammiversary, defeating Alexander in a Last Man Standing Match inside of a steel cage. But his reign lasted for just a few hours.

Later that night, Slater addressed Nemeth and told him he would be cashing in Option C. The decision allowed Slater to trade his X Division Championship in for a shot at the world title. The match was then set for Bound for Glory.

Slater has a chance to etch his name alongside TNA Wrestling legends like Kurt Angle, Christian Cage, Sting, Jeff Jarrett, Moose and Jeff Hardy. But getting past Nemeth isn’t going to be easy.

Nemeth is in the middle of his second reign. He defeated Mike Santana for the title at Slammiversary. He earned the chance after winning the Call Your Shot Gauntlet – a match that is also taking place at Bound for Glory that will see at least one wrestler earn a world title shot down the line.

Now, Nemeth has a shot to play spoiler against Slater.

Bound for Glory is set to take place at the Yuengling Center in Tampa, Florida. The action will begin at 4:30 p.m. ET and can be seen on TNA+.

item.title: WATCH: CDC director discusses US government response to Russian plague concerns: 'We are protected'
item.description: CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz says the agency is monitoring travelers from Siberia amid concerns about a pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia.
item.content:encoded:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is coordinating with federal agencies to monitor travelers entering the United States from Siberia amid concerns about a possible pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia, the agency's director revealed Wednesday.

CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz said the Trump administration is working across multiple agencies to identify travelers arriving from the region following the mysterious death of a Russian laboratory worker, while emphasizing that the risk to Americans remains minimal.

"We are very confident that the threat to the United States is extremely low," Schwartz said during a Wall Street Journal health forum Wednesday.

MOTHER OF DEAD RUSSIAN ANTI-PLAGUE INSTITUTE WORKER: 'I KNOW THE TRUTH'

The concerns stem from the Oct. 2 death of Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia, whose death has fueled speculation about a possible pneumonic plague infection.

Russian authorities have maintained that Shipilova died from pneumonia of unknown origin and have not confirmed that she was infected with Yersinia pestis, the bacteria that causes pneumonic plague.

Schwartz said the CDC is working with the departments of Homeland Security, State and War, among other federal agencies, to track potential arrivals from the region.

"There are about 200 flights that come into the United States from Siberia, that region," Schwartz said, adding that those flights typically arrive at New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport.

"We have a port health station set up in JFK so that we can do appropriate surveillance and screening if anyone from that area comes into the United States," she continued.

The CDC director stressed that while pneumonic plague is a serious bacterial infection capable of spreading between people through respiratory droplets, early detection and treatment can prevent deaths.

TRUMP RESPONDS TO CONCERNS OVER SUSPECTED PLAGUE CASE IN RUSSIA, SAYING US 'WILLING TO HELP'

"The one good thing, if I could say there's a good thing, is that it's a treatable, highly treatable bacterial disease with common antibiotics that most physicians within the United States can utilize," Schwartz said.

The illness is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and is considered the most serious form of plague, according to the CDC. Symptoms can include fever, chest pain, coughing and rapidly developing pneumonia. Without prompt antibiotic treatment, the infection can be fatal, the agency warns.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has pressed Moscow for additional information about Shipilova's death.

Russian authorities placed approximately 200 people who had contact with the deceased laboratory worker under quarantine, according to Euronews. On Thursday, Irkutsk Gov. Igor Kobzev said preventive measures had been completed and roughly 5,000 laboratory tests had detected no pathogens, according to the Associated Press.

RUSSIAN RESEARCHER'S MYSTERY DEATH COULD BE ‘FAR WORSE’ THAN THE PLAGUE, FORMER SENIOR TRUMP OFFICIAL WARNS

However, Russian officials have not publicly identified the pathogen responsible for Shipilova's pneumonia or definitively ruled out pneumonic plague as the cause of her death, according to The Associated Press.

Asked whether Moscow was being sufficiently transparent with American authorities, Schwartz indicated that the administration was still seeking answers.

"We are still having those conversations about what exactly happened in Siberia," she said, adding that U.S. officials were working with information about an unconfirmed case of pneumonic plague.

item.title: Your phone can fix badly framed photos after you take them
item.description: Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 adds Extend and Reframe tools to Photos, letting iPhones generate new background areas beyond your original borders.
item.content:encoded:
Have you ever taken a photo you really liked, only to realize later that you stood too close, cut off part of the background or framed the subject in the wrong spot? Normally, fixing that means cropping even more of the photo. Now your phone may be able to go in the other direction.

Apple added new Extend and Reframe tools to Photos in iOS 27. Instead of simply cutting away part of an image, Apple Intelligence can generate additional areas around the original shot or change its perspective after you take it. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones offer similar AI editing tools that can help rescue photos that did not come out quite the way you planned.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care . Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist .

12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW

Apple added several Apple Intelligence upgrades to Photos with iOS 27. Two of the most useful are Extend and Reframe.

Extend lets you expand a photo beyond its original borders. For example, if someone's head is too close to the top of the image or you want more space around the subject, Apple Intelligence can generate additional background.

Reframe goes further. Apple says it lets you change the point of capture after taking the photo. You can move the image, zoom, rotate it and adjust its perspective while Apple Intelligence generates the additional portions needed for the new composition.

These tools go beyond traditional cropping. Cropping removes part of your image. Extend and Reframe can create parts of the image that were never captured by the camera. Because these are generative AI features, take a close look at the final result. AI-generated areas can sometimes contain strange details, especially around faces, hands, text or complicated backgrounds.

Extend and Reframe require Apple Intelligence and iOS 27 or later.

Apple Intelligence works on:

Availability can also depend on your language and region. Apple says some Apple Intelligence features may have usage limits. If you have an older iPhone that can install iOS 27 but does not support Apple Intelligence, you will not get these particular editing tools.

Use Extend when you want more room around the subject or need to expand the edges of your original photo.

If you change your mind later, Apple lets you return to the editing tools and reset the Extend changes.

CALIFORNIA LAW PUTS DIGITAL FINGERPRINTS ON AI FAKES

Use Reframe when the composition or perspective feels wrong rather than simply too tight.

This can be especially useful when your subject is awkwardly positioned or you wish you had held the camera at a slightly different angle.

Samsung takes a somewhat different approach. Compatible Galaxy phones use Galaxy AI Photo Assist, which includes tools for moving, removing and adding objects in a photo. For this trick, the Move tool is the one to use. It lets you reposition, rotate or resize part of the image, then uses generative AI to fill in the background created by your changes. Samsung's standard Gallery editor also lets you change the aspect ratio, rotate the picture and adjust its angle.

Menus can vary slightly by Galaxy model and software version.

8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT

Google Photos has one of the closest Android alternatives to Apple's new Extend tool. It's called Auto frame. Google says Auto frame can recompose a photo that is too tightly cropped or poorly framed. It can also use AI to fill in missing areas and extend the background.

Make sure you have the latest version of the Google Photos app.

Google also includes Straighten, Rotate, Perspective and Aspect ratio controls in the same Crop section if you want to make the adjustment yourself.

Google rolls out some Photos features gradually. Therefore, if you do not see Auto frame, update Google Photos and check again. Availability can also vary by device, account and region.

AI photo editing works best when you give it a reasonably clear original image. Here are a few things to keep in mind.

AI can generate new areas around an image, but it cannot completely rescue every blurry or badly exposed shot. Start with the clearest version you have.

Instead of dramatically expanding the entire picture, try adding a little extra space around the edges. Smaller edits can look more natural.

Zoom in before saving. Check faces, hands, hair, jewelry and clothing for unexpected changes.

Generative AI can struggle with letters and numbers. Look closely at street signs, shirts, storefronts and anything else containing text.

When your phone gives you the option, save the edited version as a copy. That way, you still have the untouched photo if the AI result does not look right later.

One of the frustrating things about smartphone photography is realizing you almost got the perfect shot. Maybe you stood a little too close, left the person too far to one side or tilted the camera just enough to make the composition feel wrong. iOS 27 gives supported iPhones another way to fix those mistakes with Extend and Reframe. I also like that Galaxy and Pixel owners have comparable options instead of sitting this one out. These tools will not replace taking a well-framed photo in the first place, but they can give a photo you would otherwise delete another shot.

item.title: Innocent mistake on long flight could have devastating consequences for travelers
item.description: One traveler was diagnosed with a corneal ulcer after wearing contact lenses all throughout an 11-hour flight — prompting eye doctors to warn about cabin air risks.
item.content:encoded:
An everyday habit during a long-haul flight could have painful consequences for certain travelers — with a recent case highlighting some serious dangers. 

The dry air inside an airplane cabin, combined with hours spent wearing contact lenses during a long travel day, can leave the lenses with less moisture and eyes feeling increasingly uncomfortable, experts say.

In some cases, irritation or damage to the surface of the eye can lead to more serious problems.

FLIGHT ATTENDANTS BEG TRAVELERS TO STOP DOING THE ONE THING THAT ANNOYS CREWS MOST

One traveler recently described temporarily losing vision in one eye after returning home from an international trip, according to the New York Post.

The woman said she wore her contact lenses throughout an 11-hour flight home from Greece and for roughly 24 hours of travel — while also wearing them while swimming and showering, according to the outlet.

Within days of returning home, the traveler developed pain and sensitivity to light before her vision significantly worsened. 

Doctors eventually diagnosed her with a corneal ulcer. 

She underwent weeks of treatment with eye drops and was left with a small scar that continues to blur part of her vision, the outlet reported.

Valerie Kattouf, an Illinois-based optometrist, told Fox News Digital that wearing contacts during extended flights can increase dry-eye symptoms and lead to irritation, a "sandy, gritty feeling" and intermittent blurred vision.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"The cabin air has significantly reduced humidity that can actually remove moisture from the contact lens and create more dryness," Kattouf said.

Falling asleep during a long or overnight flight can add another concern for travelers wearing contacts.

"People often sleep on long flights, which contributes to more risk with contact [lens] wear," Kattouf said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

As a contact lens loses moisture, it may move less freely on the eye, Kattouf said. 

Removing a particularly dry lens could potentially disturb the epithelium, the outer layer of the cornea, causing significant irritation and potentially affecting vision.

For travelers preparing for a long flight, Kattouf recommends bringing an up-to-date pair of prescription glasses.

"Wearing glasses during a long flight is more ideal for eye health and long-term comfortable contact [lens] wear," she said.

As another option, travelers who begin their journey wearing contacts can switch to glasses before sleeping or partway through the flight, Kattouf suggested.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For those who keep their contacts in, single-use vials of artificial tears may also help provide additional lubrication during the flight, according to Kattouf.

The issue has also led to discussion among travelers online, with some saying they routinely opt for glasses during longer trips.

"I [always] wear glasses on long flights," one Reddit user wrote. "My eyes just feel so much more comfortable by the time I land, and I don't have to worry about taking them out at the airport or on the plane, or sleeping on the plane."

Another traveler said that leaving contacts in place during a flight left the person regretting the decision.

"My eyes were so dry at the end, even with eyedrops," the person wrote.

item.title: 'Reagan' star Lesley-Anne Down relives 3 terrifying brushes with death: ‘I should have been killed’
item.description: Lesley-Anne Down recalls three harrowing brushes with danger, including a chilling link to the Moors murders and a terrifying fake taxi escape.
item.content:encoded:
Lesley-Anne Down believes she's already used up three of her nine lives.

The actress, who takes on the Iron Lady opposite Dennis Quaid in "Reagan," has shown plenty of steel off-screen, recalling "three times in my life when I should have been killed by other people."

For Down, known for her roles in "North and South" and "Upstairs, Downstairs," the unsettling experiences began when she was just 10 years old.

MORGAN FAIRCHILD SAYS TWO MEN ONCE ABDUCTED HER OFF NYC STREET AS BYSTANDERS LAUGHED

"I remember there was a little girl, one of a number of children who were murdered and buried on the moors in England," the British star told Fox News Digital. "There was a little girl who had dark hair and blue eyes and was my age, 10. Her name was Leslie Ann Downey. My mother got phone calls when this little girl's identity was announced."

"It wasn't me, of course," said Down. "But it certainly freaked her out. Leslie Ann Downey was about six months younger than me. It turned out there were two people, a man and a woman. Ian Brady and Myra Hindley. They were the killers."

Brady and Hindley murdered five children between 1963 and 1965, with several of their victims buried on Saddleworth Moor in northern England, according to The Associated Press. The case became known as the Moors murders.

WATCH: ‘REAGAN’ PRODUCER SHARES WHAT HE LEARNED FROM RESEARCHING RONALD REAGAN

Hindley and Brady were arrested in 1965 and later convicted of murders connected to the case. The five victims were Downey, Pauline Reade, John Kilbride, Keith Bennett and Edward Evans, who ranged in age from 10 to 17. Bennett's body has never been found.

According to accounts of the case, Downey was abducted after Hindley asked her to help carry packages to a car.

Hindley died in 2002 while serving a life sentence. Brady died in a psychiatric hospital in 2017.

The case frightened Down’s family. But it wouldn’t be the last time danger came close to home.

"A year later, my mother and I were coming back from the launderette with the washing," Down said. "I ran ahead. I left the washing, I left my mother and just ran ahead. I ran uphill and then over a footbridge. As I ran over the footbridge, a man came from the other side. He's walking towards me. He stops in the middle of the footbridge and says, 'Hello.' He then was going to put me in his car."

"He told me he needed a babysitter, and he would call my parents when we got to his house," Down said. "I remember having one foot in the car. Seeing my mother broke the spell. Then he was gone. But I still remember that horrible feeling swooping in before my mother came."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Years later, when Down was 18, she ordered a taxi. But when a car pulled up in the countryside, she climbed in and quickly noticed something was wrong.

"As soon as he's driving away, I'm already feeling that horrible feeling," Down said. "I looked around and there were no radios or anything, like a taxi is supposed to have. So I said, 'Could you pull over, please?' He said, 'Oh no, we don't need to pull over. We'll be there soon.'"

Down said she decided to jump from the moving car.

"I opened the door and threw myself out of the 25-mile an hour car," she said. "I fell onto the curb in a puddle. I was covered in blood. There was nobody around. What did he do? He pulled the car door shut and drove off at top speed. I didn't freeze up because I couldn't. That feeling was familiar to me. I've been through it."

Down, now 72, earned a Golden Globe nomination for her role opposite Patrick Swayze in "North and South." She also starred opposite Peter Sellers in "The Pink Panther Strikes Again" and Harrison Ford in "Hanover Street." She later appeared on the soap opera "The Bold and the Beautiful."

When asked what advice she would give to women pursuing a career in Hollywood, Down had a warning: "Never go anywhere alone."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Always have your agent or your publicist with you at all times," she said. "Even if they have to be on the phone a lot and out in the lobby, just always have somebody with you at all times as you chase your dreams."

"I made a decision many, many years ago, actually about 2012, that I wanted out," Down said. "I was in a position where I didn't have to. Things were very good. And I was fortunate to have all my eggs in a basket and make a choice."

Down has since moved from California to Georgia. She also said she has no regrets about turning down two opportunities to play a Bond girl.

"I guess my thought process was maybe a little old-fashioned, but being a Bond girl didn't really resonate with me," she explained. "Being a Bond girl was skimpy clothing, pretty face, not much dialogue, no acting involved, kissing James at the end in a spacecraft or whatever. I thought if I became a Bond girl, then I'd be a Bond girl for life. I didn't want that for myself."

The opportunity to play Thatcher came "out of the blue," Down said. She accepted the role and said she was grateful for the experience.

"She loved and believed in England and the English people," Down said. "Her counterpart, Mr. Reagan, also believed and loved the American people."

Down said leaders should "encompass what Thatcher and Reagan both believed," including doing "anything and everything they can for the longevity and success of the nation."

For Down, taking on the role of Thatcher became another unexpected chapter in a life that has repeatedly taken surprising turns. But these days, the actress is content with where those turns have taken her.

"My choice was to live the life I’m living now," she said.

item.title: Trump announces immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
item.description: President Donald Trump declared an immediate energy ceasefire, but his recent deal easing Russian diesel exports drew sharp criticism from Kyiv.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, saying both countries have agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy infrastructure after weeks of escalating tensions over strikes on oil refineries and power plants.

"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

The announcement comes as Trump has intensified pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian oil refineries, arguing that the attacks have disrupted global diesel supplies and contributed to higher fuel prices for American consumers.

The issue has become increasingly urgent as diesel prices weigh on American farmers, truckers and businesses that rely on the fuel to transport goods and operate heavy equipment.

RECORD GAS PRICES SQUEEZE AMERICANS AS MIDTERMS LOOM AND WAR IN UKRAINE AND IRAN WAGES ON

Trump has repeatedly criticized Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities, even as Kyiv maintains that targeting Moscow's oil industry is a legitimate strategy to weaken Russia's ability to finance its war.

The announcement follows a contentious week in U.S.-Ukraine relations after Trump struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian diesel exports to reach American and global markets.

Under the agreement announced Friday, Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, with additional shipments expected in November and beyond. The Treasury Department also authorized temporary sanctions relief to facilitate Russian diesel supplies.

Trump argued that the agreement would help bring down fuel prices, while Zelenskyy criticized the decision as a concession to Moscow that could provide additional revenue for Russia's war effort.

The dispute escalated Saturday when Trump suggested Ukraine should replace Zelenskyy with a leader more willing to negotiate an end to the war.

"I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal," Trump told reporters.

'OUR POSITION IS CLEAR:' ZELENSKYY AND EU DISMISS CEDING UKRAINIAN LAND TO RUSSIA

Zelenskyy, meanwhile, has maintained that Ukraine would be willing to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow agreed to stop targeting Ukrainian power plants and other critical infrastructure.

The two countries have increasingly targeted each other's energy systems throughout the war, although the consequences have differed.

Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid have left civilians facing electricity disruptions and damaged infrastructure needed to heat homes and sustain businesses. Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, meanwhile, have disrupted fuel production and exports, putting additional pressure on global energy markets.

The Trump administration has spent weeks attempting to negotiate a reciprocal halt to energy attacks as part of broader diplomatic efforts to bring an end to the war.

In September, Trump similarly announced that both countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, although Moscow did not publicly confirm the agreement and attacks continued.

The latest announcement raises the possibility of renewed diplomatic progress, but an energy ceasefire would not amount to a comprehensive agreement to end the fighting.

It was not immediately clear how the agreement would be monitored or enforced. The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News Digital reached out to the Ukrainian and Russian embassies in Washington, D.C., seeking confirmation of the ceasefire but did not immediately receive responses.

item.title: Why verified social media accounts can still lead you into a scam
item.description: Microsoft's X account was hijacked to promote a crypto pump-and-dump scheme, exposing its more than 13 million followers to a scam campaign.
item.content:encoded:
We have all developed little shortcuts for deciding whether something online looks legitimate. You check the account name. You recognize the company logo. Then you spot that verification badge and your guard comes down a little. That can be exactly what scammers are counting on.

Microsoft’s official X account became the latest reminder after attackers gained unauthorized access and used the account in an apparent cryptocurrency pump-and-dump scheme. The account has more than 13 million followers, giving whoever controlled it access to a huge audience and the credibility that comes with Microsoft’s name.

Here is what happened, why compromised verified accounts can be so convincing and what you should check before trusting the next surprising post that shows up in your feed.

Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care . Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist .

6 CRYPTO SCAM SCRIPTS CRIMINALS USE TO STEAL YOUR MONEY

BleepingComputer reported that Microsoft's @Microsoft account followed and reposted content from another X account that appeared to be Clippy-themed. That account was promoting a cryptocurrency called $Clippy. Microsoft tells CyberGuy that two unauthorized posts appeared during the period when its account was compromised. According to the company, the first was a quote repost of content from what appeared to be a Clippy-themed account and referenced bringing back Microsoft Office's old animated paperclip character. The second appeared to be an apology related to the earlier activity. Microsoft says neither post originated from the company.

A Microsoft spokesperson provided CyberGuy with the following statement: "We have confirmed unauthorized access to our account on X, including posts that did not originate from Microsoft. The account has been secured, the unauthorized posts have been removed, and we are continuing to investigate the circumstances."

If an account you have never heard of suddenly tells you Microsoft launched a Clippy cryptocurrency, you might keep scrolling. When Microsoft’s actual account appears to amplify that same message, it becomes much easier to hesitate. You may assume someone at the company approved the post. You might click a link because you recognize the account. Someone interested in crypto could move even faster because they are worried about missing an opportunity.

That is the advantage attackers get when they compromise a well-known account. They inherit trust that has already been built for them. We recently saw the same basic weakness after hackers hijacked HBO Max’s verified Reddit account. Researchers found that attackers used the compromised account to push 108 malicious ads over roughly 48 hours. Because those ads appeared under a familiar verified account, they had an extra layer of credibility.

THOUSANDS OF HACKED SITES TRICK YOU INTO INSTALLING MALWARE

This is also not Microsoft’s first encounter with a crypto scam involving one of its X accounts. In June 2024, scammers hijacked Microsoft India’s X account and used it to impersonate Keith Gill, better known online as Roaring Kitty. The attackers then promoted what appeared to be a GameStop cryptocurrency presale.

People who followed the link and connected their cryptocurrency wallets risked having their assets stolen through wallet-draining malware. That example shows how quickly a social media takeover can turn into something much more expensive. A post may only be the beginning. The real danger often waits behind the link.

One of the clearest examples happened in January 2024 when attackers took over the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s official X account. The compromised account falsely announced that the SEC had approved spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds. According to the Justice Department, Bitcoin jumped by more than $1,000 following the false post. After the SEC regained control and corrected the announcement, Bitcoin fell by more than $2,000.

Investigators later determined that attackers gained control through a SIM swap involving the phone number associated with the SEC account. Eric Council Jr. pleaded guilty in February 2025 to conspiracy charges related to the attack and was sentenced in May 2025 to 14 months in prison. That case gives us a good example of how much influence one compromised account can have. An official-looking post can spread quickly before the real organization has time to warn everyone that something has gone wrong.

A verification badge can still be useful. It may help confirm that an account belongs to the person, company or organization it claims to represent. What it cannot tell you is whether that same organization still controls the account at the exact moment you are reading a post.

Hackers can steal credentials through phishing or take advantage of other account takeover techniques. SIM swapping has also been used to intercept password reset codes and defeat some forms of two-factor authentication. CyberGuy has covered this problem before on X, where hackers have taken over verified accounts and then changed them to impersonate cryptocurrency projects. The account may look established because it is. The person controlling it may have changed.

You do not need to assume every surprising post is the work of a hacker. Still, when an account suddenly asks you to spend money or connect something valuable, a few extra checks can save you from a painful mistake.

If a company announces a cryptocurrency, giveaway or major investment opportunity on social media, go directly to the company’s website. Look for the same announcement in its newsroom or another official channel. If the only place you can find it is one social media post, wait before acting.

If an account that normally talks about software suddenly starts pushing an obscure crypto token, treat that change as a warning sign. Scroll through its recent posts and check whether the promotion fits anything the company has announced elsewhere.

Connecting a cryptocurrency wallet can expose you to malicious approvals that allow attackers to move assets. Navigate directly to a service you already trust instead. Never enter your recovery phrase or private key into a site because a social media post tells you to.

Strong antivirus software can help warn you about phishing sites, malicious downloads and other threats that may be waiting behind a suspicious link. Security software adds another layer of protection, but it should never replace slowing down and checking where a link came from. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

Scammers love deadlines. You may be told a token is launching right now or that an offer disappears in a few minutes. That pressure is designed to get you moving before you verify what you are seeing. Give yourself time to check another source.

Even when the post comes from a legitimate account, the link inside it may lead somewhere dangerous. Look carefully at the web address before entering a password, payment information or crypto credentials. Small changes in a domain name can lead you to an entirely different site.

Use a unique password for important accounts and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). A password manager can help you create and store strong, unique passwords so you are less likely to reuse them across accounts. An authenticator app or passkey can provide stronger protection than relying only on texted security codes. Also check your account’s active sessions periodically and sign out any devices you do not recognize.

What you should do next depends on how far you got before realizing something looked suspicious.

The Microsoft attack is a good reminder of how quickly the signals we rely on can turn against us. We tell people to check the account name, look for the real profile and be cautious with impersonators. In this case, attackers briefly had control of the account people were supposed to trust. I would still use verification as one clue, but I would never let a checkmark do the thinking for me when money, passwords or a crypto wallet are involved. If a company suddenly posts something that feels out of character, verify it somewhere else before you act. Go to the company’s website, check another official channel and give yourself a minute before clicking. That extra pause can be the difference between spotting a scam and paying for one.

item.title: Minnesota GOP chair blasts progressive group over KKK-themed sign shown during Black House speaker's remarks
item.description: Sunrise Movement Twin Cities said it disrupted a Minnesota Republican Party fundraiser, displaying a "RepubliKKKan Party" banner during Lisa Demuth's remarks.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota's Republican Party chairman is accusing protesters of racial intimidation after demonstrators disrupted a GOP dinner and displayed a sign invoking the Ku Klux Klan while the state's first Black female House speaker addressed the crowd.

Minnesota GOP Chair Alex Plechash blasted the demonstrators in a statement after Friday night's Lincoln Reagan Dinner in Eagan, where protesters held a sign reading "RepubliKKKan Party" during remarks by House Speaker and Republican gubernatorial candidate Lisa Demuth.

"Last night, radical protesters stormed the stage at our Lincoln Reagan Dinner and held up a KKK symbol while Speaker Lisa Demuth spoke," Plechash said in a statement posted to X by the Republican Party of Minnesota.

DAVID MARCUS: MINNESOTA GOP CANDIDATES KEEP TRUMP AT ARM'S LENGTH AS THEY EYE A POST-TRUMP PARTY FUTURE

"Let's be clear about what happened. Left leaning protesters aimed a symbol of racial terror at a Black woman leader, at a dinner named for the president who ended slavery," he continued.

Sunrise Movement Twin Cities, a progressive activist organization, claimed responsibility for the disruption and said the demonstration was intended to protest Republican policies it believes harm immigrants and marginalized communities, according to local news station KTSP.

"We disrupted this fundraiser because we refuse to give a moment's peace to the people bankrolling racial violence," the group said in a statement cited by the outlet.

The organization also said it was not affiliated with Minnesota's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party (DFL).

Video of the incident shows demonstrators moving toward the front of the room holding signs, including one with the letters "KKK" highlighted in red, according to outlet.

One protester could be heard shouting, "You love Trump and you will not stand up for Minnesotans," as Demuth stood on stage holding a microphone.

As security escorted the demonstrators away, attendees began chanting, "Lisa," followed by chants of, "USA."

Plechash told the outlet that protesters gained access to the dinner by purchasing tickets and passing through security checkpoints.

KLOBUCHAR'S FRAUD FIGHT CLAIM TAKES HIT AFTER GOP OPPONENT COMBS THROUGH RECEIPTS: 'WHERE WERE YOU?'

The chairman said the event experienced two disruptions, the first during remarks by Republican U.S. Senate candidate Michele Tafoya and the second while Demuth was speaking.

Plechash said roughly three or four protesters pushed toward the front of the room carrying banners during Demuth's remarks. He estimated the disruption lasted about 30 seconds and said he did not believe the demonstrators posed a physical threat.

Plechash said in his X post that Eagan police issued trespass orders and that potential charges remained under investigation.

The GOP chairman also called out Minnesota Democrats, specifically naming the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party, Sen. Amy Klobuchar and Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan.

"Intimidation, criminal behavior, and racist rhetoric have no place in Minnesota politics," Plechash wrote.

"Republicans debate ideas, and we'd welcome the DFL to show up and do the same," he added. "Every hour they stay silent says something. Their silence is deafening."

Demuth, who won Minnesota's Republican gubernatorial primary in August, will face off against Klobuchar, the Democratic nominee, in November's election to succeed Gov. Tim Walz.

item.title: California city backs down on $20K daily fine threat against pastor's food pantry after outpouring of support
item.description: Matt Mahan says San Jose is offering relocation help to Lighthouse Food Rescue after a citation threatened daily fines of up to $20,000 a day.
item.content:encoded:
A California pastor who provides free groceries to more than 1,000 people daily was ordered in September to shut down his food pantry after the city of San Jose cited zoning violations and blocked sidewalks, threatening fines of up to $20,000, just a day before officials changed course following an outpouring of social media support.

Lighthouse Food Rescue & Distribution, operated by Pastfor Ralph Olmos, received a citation requiring the nonprofit to remove its food distribution operation from the public sidewalk within 10 days and cease operations at its longtime 17th Street location within 60 days.

Olmos told Fox News Digital that despite the city's subsequent offer to help with relocation costs, he sees little possibility of keeping the pantry at its current location, pointing to the city's previous recognition of his charitable work.

"I can tell you that this is definitely not my first rodeo with the City," Olmos told Fox News Digital. "But from being called a Beacon of hope, to get out or we will fine you. There really doesn't seem any way that the Lighthouse stays on 17th street."

CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR CANDIDATE WARNS OF 'MAGA-LIKE' STATE MOVEMENT UNLESS DEMS 'WAKE UP'

Following the backlash, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and Councilmember Anthony Tordillos, who represent the district where Lighthouse operates, told Fox News Digital that the city was working to help relocate the pantry while addressing concerns about sidewalk accessibility for neighborhood residents.

"Two things can be true at once – and they are in this case. Lighthouse is doing incredible work in the community and their neighbors deserve to be able to use the sidewalk," the officials said in a joint statement. 

"We’ve been working with our Housing Department and Code Compliance Team to find a place where the pastor can relocate and continue serving the community while ensuring that the mobility issues in the neighborhood are addressed so that elderly and disabled residents can get where they need to go," they added. 

The officials also addressed the potential financial penalties outlined in the city's original enforcement notice, emphasizing that no fines had been imposed and that San Jose was instead offering financial assistance to help the nonprofit relocate.

"No fines have been assessed – in fact, the City has offered to help with relocation costs because we are committed to finding a solution that is not punitive but creates a better situation for everyone involved," Mahan and Tordillos said.

DEM MAYOR FED UP WITH HOMELESS CRISIS PROPOSES JAILING VAGRANTS WHO REFUSE HOUSING

The response followed a report from San Jose Spotlight, detailing a Sept. 25 citation ordering Lighthouse to remove its sidewalk food distribution operation and canopies within 10 days or face potential fines of up to $20,000 daily. The citation also directed the nonprofit to cease operations at its current location within 60 days.

Pastor Ralph Olmos, the nonprofit's president and CEO, previously expressed concern about abandoning the families who depend on its services.

"I'm up against the wall. It's almost like (the city is) telling me to stop. But my conviction says, 'How can I leave the people?'" Olmos told San Jose Spotlight.

The pantry, located near East Julian and North 17th streets, distributes groceries five days a week to families, seniors, homeless residents and people with disabilities. Its offerings include milk, meat, eggs and specialized food packages.

WATCH: CALIFORNIA DEMS RALLY AROUND HEALTHCARE FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS DURING FIERY DEBATE

Mahan also addressed the controversy on Instagram, saying his administration was working to ensure the organization's charitable efforts continue.

"Seeing the outpouring of advocacy and support for [Light House Food Rescue] has been amazing — and I’m right there with you. Pastor Olmos has been doing incredible work in our community and we’re going to make sure that work can continue. My team, alongside our Housing Department, has been in touch with the Pastor over the past week to help them relocate to a location that works for them, the people they serve and their neighbors. The city may even be able to help them with moving costs. Stay tuned!" Mahan said.

The controversy marked another dispute between the Lighthouse and the city.

In 2022, the nonprofit faced a special use permit requirement costing up to $15,500. Following community opposition, then-Mayor Sam Liccardo and Councilmember Raul Peralez proposed waiving or funding the fees. The City Council later voted unanimously to support relief for food pantries, according to the San Jose Spotlight.

That same year, San Jose officially recognized Lighthouse through its Silicon Valley Strong Heroes initiative, praising Olmos and volunteers for feeding vulnerable residents during the pandemic.

City Planning, Building and Code Enforcement spokesperson Marika Krause told San José Spotlight that zoning rules have since changed and a special use permit is no longer available for the pantry's current operations. 

The city has not publicly confirmed a finalized relocation site or whether the original 60-day shutdown order has been rescinded.

item.title: Mysterious find beneath field leads man to massive treasure hidden for centuries
item.description: Marking the largest coin hoard from Emperor Hadrian's era ever found, a metal detector hobbyist unearthed 934 Roman silver denarii near Cologne, Germany.
item.content:encoded:
A man searching a German field with a metal detector stumbled upon a remarkable discovery.

He found 934 ancient Roman silver coins — and an expert says the nearly 2,000-year-old treasure and "huge hoard" may have been someone's life savings.

The coins, found near Wesseling, south of Cologne, were uncovered by Oliver Riedl, according to The Associated Press (AP). Though the hoard was discovered last year, officials only recently announced the find, calling it the largest coin hoard from the reign of Roman Emperor Hadrian ever found in Germany.

PUZZLING SOUND IN BACKYARD LEADS HOMEOWNER TO MASSIVE 1,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE

A licensed metal detectorist, Riedl immediately alerted archaeological authorities after realizing more coins were buried beneath the surface.

The hobbyist told the AP he suspected there were more coins beneath the surface after his metal detector continued picking up signals.

"It was clear to me there was something bigger buried here," he said.

Pictures show the ancient Roman silver denarii after they were carefully cleaned, some bearing portraits and inscriptions.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MASSIVE ANCIENT SITE DURING RAIL PROJECT, INCLUDING RARE ROMAN FIND

The coins were likely buried intentionally between 125 and 150 A.D., according to the LVR Office for the Preservation of Archaeological Monuments in the Rhineland.

The staggering hoard weighs 6.8 pounds and is currently on display at the LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn.

The most striking aspect of the hoard was its unusual size, said Johannes Wienand, a professor of ancient history at the Technical University of Braunschweig in Germany.

Wienand was not involved in the discovery or its research but told Fox News Digital the hoard is "a huge treasure."

POLICE OFFICERS SPOT STRANGE OBJECTS UNDERWATER, THEN MAKE REMARKABLE ANCIENT DISCOVERY

"It's certainly the largest Roman coin hoard of that sort from Hadrian's time," he said.

"It's a time capsule of the money the people in that period actually used day by day."

A Roman legionary would have earned a gross salary of around 300 denarii per year, Wienand said, meaning the hoard was roughly equivalent to three years of a soldier's gross salary.

"A Roman soldier would need six, seven, eight, even more years to save this amount of money, maybe for his retirement," he said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The coins were discovered in a rural area near the Rhine frontier, which marked a border of the Roman Empire at the time, he noted. The Roman city of Cologne and a legionary fortress in Bonn were also nearby — raising the possibility of a military connection.

While a military connection is possible, Wienand said the identity of the hoard's owner remains unknown.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"It seems to have been the life savings of one person who put this treasure together and put it in a pot, buried it in the soil to save it for later," Wienand said.

"And obviously the owner was never able to recover this treasure."

Above all, Wienand said the discovery highlights the importance of responsible metal detecting and reporting archaeological finds.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"It's actually a story of how to do things right," he said. "The metal detectorist was licensed. He had permission to look for finds like that. He immediately called the heritage officers."

Wienand added, "He reported the find, and he contributed to an orderly exploration of this remarkable find."

"These coins and this hoard [are] now part of our cultural heritage. And I think that's a very good outcome of this story."

The Associated Press contributed reporting.

item.title: Silent inflammation could be damaging your body — and 5 habits may help keep it in check

Inflammation is a natural immune response that helps protect the body from injury and infection, but when it becomes chronic, it can pose a health threat, according to the National Institutes of Health.

Over time, chronic inflammation can contribute to rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, inflammatory bowel disease and cardiovascular disease.

Keeping the condition in check can help protect healthy tissues and support overall health, experts say.

Jim LaValle, a clinical pharmacist and metabolic medicine expert based in Texas, told Fox News Digital that inflammation can be influenced by a variety of factors beyond injury or infection.

LaValle first pointed to the gut-immune-brain connection — the communication between gut microbes, the immune system and the central nervous system — as one pathway that can influence the body's inflammatory response.

Beyond gut health, he said several everyday lifestyle factors can play a role in preventing chronic inflammation.

Managing stress and anxiety can help support the gut-brain connection and keep inflammation in check, according to LaValle.

He pointed to cortisol, a hormone released in response to stress, which he said can "wreak havoc on your chemistry" when levels remain elevated.

Chronic stress can also affect the intestinal barrier, potentially allowing substances that would normally remain inside the gut to pass through more easily, LaValle said.

This increased intestinal permeability is sometimes called "leaky gut."

"So, it turns out that if I'm stressed out a lot, I can be more prone to irritable bowel," LaValle said, as stress can trigger or worsen digestive symptoms in some people.

Diets high in sugar, fat and ultraprocessed foods can also affect gut health.

Paying attention to which foods trigger certain symptoms may help identify potential food sensitivities or intolerances, LaValle noted.

Symptoms such as bloating, rashes or discomfort after eating certain foods may signal a food-related reaction, although they can have other causes.

Certain medications, including antibiotics, may also alter the gut microbiome, but their effects vary depending on the drug and the individual, the expert said.

Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels is another important factor in managing inflammation, according to LaValle.

LaValle noted that conditions such as diabetes and insulin resistance are often associated with chronic inflammation.

Research suggests that GLP-1 medications, commonly prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, may have anti-inflammatory effects, while scientists are investigating other potential benefits beyond weight loss and blood sugar control.

The "exposome," or the environmental exposures people experience throughout their lives, can influence inflammation and the risk of chronic disease, according to the National Institutes of Health.

LaValle pointed to emerging research on how environmental exposures — including "forever chemicals," microplastics, metals and pesticides — may affect weight, blood sugar regulation and other aspects of health.
